---
title: "Code"
subtitle: "Inline code and fenced blocks"
---

Inline code uses IBM Plex Mono on the highlight token. Fenced blocks keep a
transparent fill, a 1px border, and a 5px radius, with padding that leaves
the copy control clear of the first line. Copy stays Quarto's control.
Long lines scroll inside the block instead of widening the page.

An inline sample is `qdk-html`.

```python
def describe_reading_surface(theme: str, width: int) -> str:
    return f"{theme} surface at {width}px retains local overflow boundaries"

long_line = "qdk keeps this intentionally long source line in a local preformatted scroll area rather than allowing it to widen the whole page beyond the reader viewport"
print(describe_reading_surface("dark", 360), long_line)
```

```{.python filename="reading.py"}
def quiet(width: int) -> str:
    return f"measure {width}px"
```

## Limits

The theme contains a long source line by scrolling inside the fenced block.
Do not wrap a paragraph in a code fence to force a measure; prose belongs in
the article, and a fence is for source.
